related_questions.question: How long are you contagious with COVID?
related_questions.snippet: People with COVID-19 can be infectious from 1–2 days before and up to 8–10 days after symptoms begin. The majority of transmission appears to occur during the early periods of infection, particularly in the 1–2 days before symptoms start and within the first few days of symptom onset.

related_questions.question: What do I do if I test positive for COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: If you test positive for COVID-19, isolate yourself to prevent further spread, contact your healthcare provider, and monitor your symptoms, seeking immediate medical attention for severe symptoms like difficulty breathing. Over-the-counter medications can help manage symptoms, and rest and hydration are important.
snippet_highlighted_words: isolate yourself to prevent further spread, contact your healthcare provider, and monitor your symptoms, seeking immediate medical attention for severe symptoms like difficulty breathing

list.title: Isolate:
list.snippet: Stay away from others to prevent transmission. Follow local guidelines for isolation duration.

list.title: Inform:
list.snippet: Notify your close contacts and your workplace or school about your positive test result.

list.title: Contact your doctor:
list.snippet: Inform your healthcare provider about your positive test result. They can assess your condition and provide specific guidance, including whether you need further treatment.

list.title: Monitor symptoms:
list.snippet: Pay close attention to any new or worsening symptoms. Report any concerns to your healthcare provider.
Rest and Hydration: Get plenty of rest and drink fluids to help your body recover.
Over-the-counter medications: Medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help manage fever and body aches.

text_blocks.snippet: 4. Seek Emergency Care for Severe Symptoms:

list.snippet: If you experience severe symptoms: Difficulty breathing, persistent chest pain or pressure, confusion, or other emergency warning signs, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room.
Check for specific recommendations: Refer to local health guidelines for isolation periods and other recommendations related to COVID-19.
